conventions: exactly one envelope object on stdout per invocation; progress is on stderr
dollar figures are estimates derived from published rates, never an invoice
an unpriced line item omits `usd` rather than reporting zero
`data.kind` carries the daemon's own status name when the exit code is coarser than the failure (ERR_PROTOCOL covers five)

`exec --stream` is the one exception to the line above: it writes NDJSON — one event object per line — and this envelope as the final line, with the discriminant `microvm.exec.stream` rather than `microvm.exec`. Every other invocation writes exactly one object

error.data: object — partial results, e.g. leaked identifiers, and `kind` naming the daemon status when one produced the failure
error.error: string — human readable, may be reworded between releases
error.exitCode: integer — matches the process exit code
error.finding: string — the docs/PLATFORM.md section, or empty

exitCodes.meaning: the command did what it said
an exception no handler claimed — a bug in this CLI, not the platform
the request was refused locally, before any AWS call
a transient condition; run the identical command again
an identity is wrong or absent; waiting will not fix it
the daemon rejected the request on its merits
the image build was never scheduled — the clientToken replay signature

exitCodes.finding: `runHookPayload` arrives wrapped, not as the body
exitCodes.meaning: the MicroVM reached a terminal state before RUNNING; read stateReason
the launch-time suspended window passed, so there is nothing to resume
a control-plane failure with no more specific class
a client-side deadline elapsed; the VM and the exec are untouched

exitCodes.finding: The build log group survives Terraform
exitCodes.meaning: interrupted after launch; teardown ran and any leak is named in the payload
a prerequisite is missing — run `microvm doctor`
the sandbox worked and the command in it exited non-zero
the VM name is registered to a live VM; refused locally, before any AWS call
the project config file is missing, malformed, or out of domain; refused locally — fix the file, or pass --no-config
run <DIR> could not pack the directory or write an artifact back; the failure is on this machine's filesystem, not the platform's
